name: Dropbox
summary: Dropbox offers a secure cloud storage API utilizing OAuth 2.0; Composio supports Dropbox integrations using either a Composio-managed OAuth flow or user-supplied Dropbox app credentials.
decision: Use the Composio-managed OAuth flow for Dropbox unless you specifically want to create and supply your own Dropbox app credentials; either way, you must ensure the Dropbox app’s callback matches the current Composio auth-config redirect URL.

setup_path.label: Use Composio-managed OAuth by default or provide your own Dropbox OAuth app credentials if desired
setup_path.note: Composio-managed authentication is the standard; custom (bring-your-own) app credentials are also supported and documented.

difficulty.value: Easy for managed OAuth; more involved if using your own app credentials (Dropbox app registration, permission selection, redirect URI configuration).
difficulty.note: Managed OAuth requires only approval and connecting via Composio; own app requires Dropbox console setup and credential management.

active_effort.note: The cited pages do not contain that duration.

approval_wait.value: App review may be required if you request broad Dropbox scopes during app registration.
approval_wait.note: Dropbox may require additional review for custom apps with wide permissions.

composio.decision: Use the Composio-managed OAuth flow for Dropbox unless you specifically want to create and supply your own Dropbox app credentials; either way, you must ensure the Dropbox app’s callback matches the current Composio auth-config redirect URL.

managed.value: Yes, Composio-managed OAuth is available for Dropbox.

bring_your_own.value: Yes, you can configure Composio to use your own Dropbox OAuth app credentials if preferred.

redirect_uri.value: the exact callback shown by the current Composio auth-config flow
redirect_uri.note: Do not use legacy or example callback values—use the callback URL exactly as shown in the latest Composio OAuth setup.

prerequisites.title: Dropbox account
prerequisites.body: You must have a Dropbox account to register a Dropbox app or connect to Dropbox via OAuth.
prerequisites.note: The cited page adds a condition this claim omits: If you'd like to quickly test out the Dropbox APIs using your own Dropbox account before implementing OAuth, you can generate an access token from your newly created app in [My apps](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps) by pressing the button that says "Generate" in the OAuth 2 section of your a

prerequisites.title: Composio access
prerequisites.body: Access to Composio via integration, SDK, or account.
prerequisites.note: Integrating Composio-managed toolkits requires Composio platform access.

steps.title: If using your own Dropbox app, register it
steps.body: Go to the Dropbox App Console (https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps) and create a new app. During registration, select permissions, scopes, and whether the app will access only its own directory or the full Dropbox. Obtain your app key and secret.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI in Dropbox app settings
steps.body: Configure the Dropbox app with the exact callback shown by the current Composio auth-config flow in the redirect URI field of the app settings. Do not use old or legacy redirect examples.

steps.title: Select appropriate API scopes and access level
steps.body: In the Dropbox app's permissions tab, choose the minimum scopes and data access level (App Folder or Full Dropbox) your integration requires.
steps.note: Request only the permissions your integration strictly needs to avoid unnecessary review or declined requests.

steps.title: Provide your Dropbox app credentials to Composio (if not managed OAuth)
steps.body: In the Composio OAuth flow or configuration for Dropbox, supply your App Key and Secret as shown in the Dropbox App Console.
steps.note: Skip this step if you are using Composio-managed OAuth.

steps.title: Connect your Dropbox account through Composio
steps.body: Use Composio’s UI or SDK to connect Dropbox. You will be redirected to Dropbox’s login and consent page and asked to approve the requested permissions.

human_actions.title: Approve Dropbox OAuth authorization request
human_actions.body: After starting the connection, approve the Dropbox OAuth consent screen to grant Composio (or your app) access to your Dropbox data.

human_actions.title: Set redirect URI in Dropbox app (if using own app)
human_actions.body: If registering your own app, manually set the redirect URI in Dropbox to exactly match the current Composio auth-config flow value.

human_actions.title: Register and configure a Dropbox app (bring your own option)
human_actions.body: As part of using your own credentials, a human must complete registration and configuration in the Dropbox App Console.
